hints.S14_A1: The dash explains it: EVERY DETAIL PERFECTLY CAPTURED AND COMPOSED, and the photos are compared to PAINTINGS. Ask: does that sound blurry, ordinary or dark - or like a work of art? Match the adjective to the praise.
hints.S14_A2: He is CAREFULLY ARRANGING the stamps BY COUNTRY AND YEAR. Ask: is that destroying them, losing them, or putting them into a neat order? Three of the choices would ruin a COLLECTION rather than build one.
hints.S14_A3: The model ship is BROKEN, and Kai spent the WHOLE WEEKEND on it. Ask: which phrasal verb means to repair something damaged? 'Give up on' means to stop trying and 'put off' means to delay - neither mends anything.
hints.S14_A4: The dash spells it out: the HAPPIEST MOMENT of her school year. Ask: does this idiom describe illness, trouble or confusion - or joy at its very highest? An idiom cannot be worked out word by word.
hints.S14_A5: The rose bushes are OVERGROWN, and the purpose is that NEW, HEALTHY FLOWERS can grow. Ask: which verb means to cut branches back? 'Watered' and 'planted' add to a plant, and 'buried' would put it underground.
hints.S14_B1: The subject is NOBODY, not the members of the CLUB. Words like nobody and everyone count as ONE person. Ask: in the present tense, does a singular subject take the plain verb, or the one ending in -s?
hints.S14_B2: HAS plus SINCE she JOINED LAST JANUARY = something begun in the past that still counts today. Ask: which form must follow 'has' - the plain verb, the -s form, the -ing form, or the past participle? This verb is irregular.
hints.S14_B3: The kite string SNAPPED SUDDENLY, cutting across something already going on, and the subject is one boy. Ask: which form shows an action still in progress in the past, and which helper goes with a singular subject?
hints.S14_B4: THAN sets her LATEST photograph against her earliest one - just two things compared. Ask: does a short adjective add -er, or take 'most' in front? And 'more' together with an -er ending is always wrong.
hints.S14_B5: The blank links two things true at the SAME MOMENT: the QUIET library, and the moment they ARRIVED at eight o'clock. Ask: could our arrival really be the REASON for the silence? A reason word makes no sense here.
hints.S14_B6: The main clause runs on IS ('Having a hobby IS important'), and it is positive. Ask: does a positive statement take a positive tag, or a negative one? The tag must echo the same verb rather than borrow 'does'.
hints.S14_B7: Her enjoyment comes first; finishing A WHOLE BOOK IN A SINGLE AFTERNOON is what follows from it. Ask: which joining word introduces a result rather than a reason? 'Because' would turn the result into the cause.
hints.S14_B8: The blank sits right before the noun CAMERAS, so it must show who owns them. Ask: can the subject pronoun 'they' ever describe a noun? A possessive form is needed - not the standalone kind that ends a sentence.
hints.S14_C1: The verb LOVES stands right in front of the blank. Ask: after love, like or enjoy, does the next verb take 'to', or the -ing ending? LOVE + verb-ing is fixed - it never takes an infinitive.
hints.S14_C2: ONE BOOK A WEEK during the school term = a habit repeated again and again, and the subject is a single person. Ask: in the simple present, what does a singular subject add to the plain verb?
hints.S14_C3: LAST HOLIDAYS puts this in finished past time. Ask: is this verb regular or irregular? Its past form is spelt exactly like the present form but is said like 'red' - so no -ed is ever added.
hints.S14_C4: WHILE signals a longer action already under way when the BUTTERFLY LANDED ON THE PAGE, and the subject counts as ONE girl. Ask: which past form shows an action in progress - a finished simple past, or a helper plus the -ing form?
hints.S14_C5: The subject SEVERAL OF HER FRIENDS names more than one person, and they all did it in that same past week. Ask: which helper does a plural subject need in the past continuous - the singular one, or the plural one?
hints.S14_C6: THEIR TEACHER REMINDED THEM - and after 'remind someone', English uses the infinitive. Ask: which little word must come before the base verb here? The -ing form can never follow 'reminded them'.
hints.S14_C7: She turns to her FAVOURITE STORIES once more when she MISSES THE CHARACTERS - she has met them before. Ask: which prefix means 'again', the one you see in replay, rewrite and rebuild? 'To' is already there, so keep the base form.
hints.S14_C8: RIGHT NOW - she does it at this very moment, aloud to her BABY SISTER. Ask: which form shows an action happening as we speak, and which helper goes with a singular subject - the singular one, or the plural one?
hints.S14_D1: The paintings are put up IN THE SCHOOL HALL FOR EVERYONE TO SEE, so the blank must be a past verb. Ask: which box word means to show artworks publicly? A 'gallery' is a place, not an action.
hints.S14_D2: The proof follows: NO TWO PAINTINGS LOOKED THE SAME. Ask: which box word describes someone who keeps producing fresh, original ideas? The blank comes after 'so', so it must be a describing word, not a noun.
hints.S14_D3: Visitors stood LONGEST in front of it, and it had taken him TWO WHOLE YEARS to finish. Ask: which box word names an artist's single greatest work? A 'portrait' shows a person - but this canvas shows a RIVER.
hints.S14_D4: The clue is IN PENCIL, in a small NOTEBOOK, before the real painting existed. Ask: which box word means to make a quick, rough drawing? It must be a past verb, because 'had first' comes in front of it.
hints.S14_D5: The RIVER REMINDED him of his HAPPIEST CHILDHOOD MEMORIES, and that is what made him want to paint. Ask: which box word means to fill someone with the urge to create? It follows 'had', so use the past participle.
hints.S14_E1: The underlined word means 'at this place', but the sentence is about the BUZZ OF EXCITEMENT reaching your ears. Ask: which spelling belongs to the ears? The two sound identical, so choose by meaning.
hints.S14_E2: Mei went into the PHOTOGRAPHY CORNER - the verb is right in meaning but wrong in spelling. Ask: how many -d- does this word really need? The base word already ends in -n, so nothing is doubled; add the past ending just once.
hints.S14_E3: The underlined word is describing RAN - an action, not a thing. Ask: do we describe HOW an action is done with an adjective, or with an adverb? A child can be quick; the way she runs needs the -ly ending.
hints.S14_E4: Find the real subject: ONE DISPLAY of handmade ITEMS. Ask: which noun is the main one - the DISPLAY, or the items inside the 'of' phrase? Match the verb to the main noun, never to the nearest word.
hints.S14_E5: The FEEDBACK FORMS belong to the students - many of them, not one. Ask: does a plain -s show ownership, or does it only make a plural? Work out where the apostrophe must sit when the owners are many.
hints.S14_F1: The PHOTOGRAPHY TEACHER is reporting a yes/no question. Ask three things: which little linking word must follow ASKED? Does the reported question keep question word order, or normal statement order? And what happens to 'you'?
hints.S14_F2: Kai was in the middle of one action when the other happened all at once. Ask: which of the two is the long background action, and which one cuts in? WHEN goes in front of the sudden event - and never drop the helping verb.
